# cad.place

> A free 3D CAD viewer that runs in the web browser. It opens STEP, IGES and BREP assemblies, meshes (STL, OBJ, PLY, OFF, 3MF, glTF, GLB) and 2D drawings (DXF, DWG), drawn with WebGPU or WebGL. A file opened from the device stays on the device: it is read in the browser and never uploaded. Tools: measure, section, explode, hole list, clearance, display styles, share-a-view links and model lists for a site's own models.

The viewer is driven by its address, so a link can open a model at a chosen view with no account and no API. Every example below is a link a user can open as it is, once the placeholder URL is replaced by a real one.

## Open a model from a URL: `?src=`

`https://cad.place/?src=<url of the file>` opens one file. Any format above is read (`.stp`, `.step`, `.igs`, `.iges`, `.brep`, `.cadmesh`, `.stl`, `.obj`, `.ply`, `.off`, `.3mf`, `.glb`, `.gltf`, `.dxf`, `.dwg`, `.zip`). The file's host must send CORS headers (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin`), because the browser fetches it from the viewer's page. When it does not, the viewer says so; the user can download the file and drop it on cad.place instead.

Example: `https://cad.place/?src=https://example.com/parts/bracket.step`

## Offer a set of models: `?list=`

`https://cad.place/?list=<url of a JSON list>` opens a site's own models, browsable from File > Browse models. The list maps each file, resolved against the list's own URL, to the name shown, in order: `{"bracket.step": "Bracket", "case.stl": "Case"}`. A name may instead be an object with `"name"` and optional `"orient"`, `"step"` (the source CAD file offered for download), `"page"`, `"links"` and `"image"`. The list's host and the models' host must send CORS headers.

Example: `https://cad.place/?list=https://example.com/models/models.json`

## Check a list before publishing it: `check?list=`

`https://cad.place/check?list=<url of a JSON list>` (also reached as `check.html?list=`) fetches each entry's model, picture, STEP file and tours the way the viewer does, and reports each check with its verdict and the URL tried (answered, CORS, found, size, format).

Example: `https://cad.place/check?list=https://example.com/models/models.json`

## Share a view: `#view=`

File > Copy view link copies a link that opens the model at the current view: camera, projection, orientation, display style, section, explode, and hidden and selected parts. The view is the `#view=` part after the model's address. It is generated by the viewer; copy it from there rather than writing it by hand.

Example shape: `https://cad.place/?src=https://example.com/parts/bracket.step#view=<copied from File > Copy view link>`

## Turn a model the right way up: `?orient=`

`?orient=` says which of the file's axes points up and which faces the viewer: any two of `up`, `front` and `right`, each `+x`, `-x`, `+y`, `-y`, `+z` or `-z`, perpendicular. The view presets (Front, Top, Iso) are taken in that frame. A file drawn Z up: `up:+z,front:-y`.

Example: `https://cad.place/?src=https://example.com/parts/bracket.step&orient=up:+z,front:-y`

## Choose the renderer: `?backend=`

`?backend=webgpu`, `webgl2` or `webgl1` forces one renderer. Without it the viewer tries them in that order and the ? box names the one in use.

Example: `https://cad.place/?src=https://example.com/parts/bracket.step&backend=webgl2`

## Embed a model in a page: `?embed=1`

`?embed=1` with `src=` (and any `list=`) shows the model alone for an `<iframe>`: no toolbar or parts panel, with Fit, full screen and a link to open it in cad.place.

Example: `<iframe src="https://cad.place/?embed=1&src=https://example.com/parts/bracket.step" width="800" height="600"></iframe>`
